reasons: Cited text supports the compliant claim: § 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor (only notice plus assignee assumption), matching the preferred carve-out.

§ 24.2 restricts Vendor asymmetrically (assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control require our prior written consent, reasonableness limited to capability/financial standing) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor absent our consent.

§ 24.4 expressly negates any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing, fee-acceleration or service-reduction right on Customer's change of control, eliminating the walk-away trigger; § 24.3's residual consent requirement is scoped to "other assignments" and does not erode § 24.1.
§ 13.3 aligns licence transfer rights with Section 24 permitted assignments, and no deemed-assignment or other change-of-control trigger favouring Vendor is cited.
No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding, and the deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out is present.
